messages:
alex: quick brain dump — thinking about a small cooperative 'hot-chunk packer' to reduce fragmentation without global stops. idea: each tenant/arena has a lightweight pack agent that compacts hot allocations into contiguous 'chunks' during low-util windows.

maria: sounds promising. goal = fewer split pages and fewer cross-page kv-cache lookups?

alex: yep. primary targets: tiny/short-lived tensors that scatter; secondary: medium-lived hot runs. reduces pointer-chasing for attention caches.

sam: how do we move live allocations without pausing inference? sounds risky for KV cache refs and GPU pointers.

alex: keep it cooperative. packer asks alloc owner for a migration token, owner yields after finishing in-flight batches. migration sequence:

```
1) packer marks dest chunk allocated
2) owner drains/serializes ephemeral refs
3) owner copies pages (async DMA) into dest
4) atomic swap of chunk descriptor + update KVCACHE refs
5) release old chunk to free list
```

maria: step 4 is tricky — atomic swap needs to be visible to all in-flight contexts. we should have a short fenced epoch. maybe use sub-epoch numbers on descriptors and let runtime check epoch on lookup.

sam: epoch approach ok, but need to bound stall time. how do we make copy fast enough? gpu->gpu memcpy for same device, otherwise GPUDirect to host then back?

lee: additivity: packer should prefer same-device targets. remote targets only if host-level fragmentation is insane. also use `cudaMemcpyAsync` + stream sync to keep latency low.

alex: agree. also want to avoid increasing memory high-water — packer should only run when slack > threshold or when it can free enough after move. we can estimate copy cost vs expected future allocation savings.

maria: what about tenant fairness? we don't want packer to monopolize DMA or cause cross-tenant noise. packer should be tenant-aware and rate-limited by tenant quota.

sam: also metadata: maintain compacted-chunk metadata per arena: base_addr, length, epoch, tenant_id, hot_score. need cheap hot_score bump on alloc/free or access sample.

lee: observability: emit per-pack metrics: bytes_moved, copies/sec, avg_copy_latency, pre/post fragmentation heatmap. useful to correlate with regressed tail latency.

alex: failure modes: 1) copy fails mid-migrate -> fallback to marking chunk pinned and abort future pack attempts; 2) epoch mismatch during swap -> retry next epoch; 3) insufficient slack -> abort. documentable.

maria: API surface? propose internal RPC `request_migration(chunk_id) -> migration_token` and owner side `complete_migration(token, new_desc)`; keep both internal in allocator layer.

sam: need tests: microbench for small tensors under bursty traffic, integration with kvcache and live model serving, chaos inject copy failures + epoch races.

lee: ops-bot: can we add a runtime flag to gate packer? `--pack-hot-chunks=[off|auto|aggressive]` and tenant-level override.

infra-bot: deploy config note: packer uses additional host pinned staging when inter-device; ensure host-pinned pool cap defaults to 0.1 * GPU_mem unless private deployment overrides.

alex: next steps: I'll write a one-pager RFC with diagrams (owner handshake, epoch swap, failure paths) and a reference handshake snippet. volunteers for review?

maria: I'll review. can also wire observability if you want.

sam: can help with kvcache integration tests.

lee: happy to prototype copy routine and evaluate stream contention.

alex: thanks. I'll post RFC draft in #eng-runtime in 24h. :+1:
